### Preparation of Aldehyde

**Addition of water:** Ethanal is produced when a solution of $20\%$ sulfuric acid and $2\%$ mercuric sulfate are added to ethyne at $80^\circ\text{C}$ temperature.

$$\text{CH}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow[80^\circ\text{C}]{20\% \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4, 2\% \text{ HgSO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$$
Ethyne $\quad\quad$ Water $\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad$ Ethanal

**Formalin:** $40\%$ of the liquid solution of formaldehyde is called formalin. Formalin contains $40\%$ methanol and $60\%$ water. Formalin is widely used in laboratories. It is used for preserving the dead bodies of different animals.

The compounds which have carboxylic group ($\text{-COOH}$) are called Organic acids or Fatty Acids. General formula of fatty acid is $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+1}\text{COOH}$. It is symbolized by $\text{R-COOH}$ in short.

**Naming:** Fatty Acids are named by omitting 'e' and adding (oic acid) with the names of Alkanes. Example: Ethanoic acid.
